Parliamentary Service Amendment (Freedom of Information) Bill 2013 — Third Reading — Read a third time

Introduced a bill to restore the exemption of three parliamentary departments from the Freedom of Information Act, explaining the exemption was inadvertently removed when a separate parliamentary service was created in 1999, and said the change is an interim measure pending a review of the 2010 FOI reforms.

Backed the bill restoring the parliamentary departments' exemption from the Freedom of Information Act, describing the difficult position the Parliamentary Librarian had been placed in after the Information Commissioner ruled the library was covered, and noted the librarian wrote to all members and senators in January 2003 raising concerns about the confidentiality of her advice.

Thanked the opposition for supporting passage of the Parliamentary Service Amendment (Freedom of Information) Bill, describing the confidentiality of Parliamentary Library advice to members as sacrosanct, and said the change restores the status quo pending consideration of the Hawke review's recommendations.

The speaker opposed the Parliamentary Service Amendment (Freedom of Information) Bill 2013, arguing it would undermine transparency by restoring FOI exemptions for three parliamentary departments, and proposed amendments to keep them subject to FOI for administrative matters and MPs' pay and expenditure.
